about: Steelbound Brewery & Distillery opened in Ellicottville in May 2018, in the ski country south of Buffalo, and set out to be one of the first places in New York State with a brewery, distillery, bar and restaurant under one roof. Co-owner Bill Bursee has since expanded to Springville and Dunkirk, with plans for a larger production plant. The brewery turns out dozens of beers a month, and the distillery makes whiskey, vodka, gin, rum and moonshine alongside its agave spirits.

Steelbound’s agave spirits are an unusual hybrid that the distillery calls a New York-style tequila: 75 percent New York corn and 25 percent Mexican blue agave, made by a process it spent more than a year developing. Made in New York and only partly from agave, it is sold as an agave spirit rather than tequila. For the Reposado, the spirit rests three months in new, charred American white oak barrels, the same kind of cask used for bourbon.

Three months is a typical rest for a reposado, long enough for the wood to round off the young spirit without masking it. The new oak gives the spirit a soft bronze color. Steelbound describes a light caramel note, a hint of smoke and a subtle, sweet white-pepper finish, and suggests drinking it neat or in cocktails. It won a bronze medal at the 2021 Great American International Spirits Competition.
